text:
Maria (Support): Customer reports: after our SSO provider changed session attributes, a subset of users are being prompted for MFA on almost every page navigation. Happening across web and embedded apps. Customer: acme-markets. They say it started ~10:00 UTC after an IdP config change.

Sam (Eng): Can you paste the exact repro steps they gave?

Maria (Support): Yep. Steps from customer: 1) login via SSO -> complete MFA; 2) load dashboard -> navigate to projects -> click into model detail -> at random page load get an immediate MFA modal instead of being treated as authenticated. Happens in both Chrome and Safari. Happens more frequently when using embedded editor.

Maria (Support): They recorded a trace. Key bits: Set-Cookie from our API response: 
```
Set-Cookie: rwd_session=eyJ...; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Max-Age=3600
```
But when they login via IdP directly, IdP sets: 
```
Set-Cookie: idp_session=...; Path=/; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=None; Max-Age=7200
```
They suspect the SameSite change at IdP causes cross-site embeddeds to drop our session cookie intermittently.

Lee (SRE): Interesting. If the site is embedded (cross-site), SameSite=Lax could be dropped for some navigations. Lax prevents sending cookies on some cross-site subrequests. That could explain intermittent reauth. Do we set any explicit cookie attributes for the device-trust token?

Sam (Eng): Our device trust flow uses two artifacts: rwd_session (session cookie) and device_jwt (localStorage). The session cookie is what gates server-side checks and lifetime. device_jwt is used by client to avoid prompting but server still validates session cookie every request. If cookie not sent, server returns 401 -> client shows MFA modal.

Olivia (Security): @Sam can you check cookie SameSite value in our auth proxy config? Also we should confirm we don't depend on cross-site cookie semantics for security decision — relying on localStorage alone is not safe.

Sam (Eng): Checking repo infra/auth-proxy/conf.yaml — current snippet: 
```
cookie:
  name: rwd_session
  secure: true
  http_only: true
  same_site: Lax
  max_age: 3600
```
We set SameSite=Lax intentionally, but older docs recommended None for embedded flows. Not comfortable changing to None without CSRF mitigations.

Maria (Support): Customer says their embedded use-case requires cross-site cookie. They want us to avoid repeated MFA until we can reach a safer long-term fix. Any temp workaround?

Lee (SRE): Short-term options: 1) advise customer to host embed on same site (subdomain) and use proper cookie domain; 2) we can issue a different cookie with SameSite=None for embed endpoints only (subpath /embed); 3) suggest they set P3P? (lol) 4) fallback: increase reliance on device_jwt header as bearer for embedded requests.

Sam (Eng): Option 2 is doable: add a separate cookie rwd_embed with SameSite=None; Secure; HttpOnly; Path=/embed. But need to coordinate with security for CSRF risk. Also need to ensure it doesn't overlap with rwd_session.

Olivia (Security): Quick checklist before issuing SameSite=None: ensure Strict CSRF tokens on state-mutating endpoints, validate Origin header on sensitive endpoints, and add double-submit cookie or anti-forgery header checks. If we can't implement all immediately, we may still temporarily serve SameSite=None with limited scope and aggressive monitoring.

Maria (Support): Customer is OK with a scoped temporary change on /embed until they adopt an iframe postMessage auth shim. They want an ETA.

Sam (Eng): I can prototype rwd_embed in the proxy today. Plan: add cookie on auth callback when query param embed=true is present. Scope to Path=/embed and set SameSite=None; Max-Age=86400. Then modify client to send device_jwt in Authorization header for embed requests.

Lee (SRE): Before rollout, let's add a canary in us-west-2 and a feature flag to toggle. I'll prepare a healthcheck and an alert on 401 spikes and increased MFA prompts (we have metrics for mfa.prompt.count).

deploy-bot: deploy request: refs/heads/feature/embed-cookie -> staging (canary us-west-2) by Sam. CI passed. :rocket:

Sam (Eng): Pushing PR now, will include logging: when we set rwd_embed we'll emit a metric `auth.embed_cookie.set` with customer_org tag. Also log the cookie attributes in debug only.

Olivia (Security): Approving temporary limited rollout on staging + canary. Post-rollout required: 1) run a 24h audit for csrf.* anomalies; 2) review with infra team to add stricter origin checks in 2 weeks; 3) schedule a follow-up with customer to migrate to postMessage flow.

Maria (Support): I'll tell the customer: short-term change scoped to /embed on canary, then 24h monitor, plan to extend if ok. Will also give them the client-side workaround (send device_jwt in Authorization header).

Sam (Eng): ETA: prototype + tests in 2 hours, canary deploy by EOW if reviews go smooth. If we hit unexpected 401 spike we'll rollback immediately.

Lee (SRE): I'll attach a runbook: if we see >2x baseline for mfa.prompt.count in 15m, rollback. Also check distributed tracing for `auth-proxy` latency.

Maria (Support): Thanks all — keeping ticket #6427 updated. Adding customer rep to thread. :+1:

Olivia (Security): After canary, we should add a permanent fix: either move to an explicit postMessage handshake (recommended) or adjust our session model so device_jwt is the primary auth for embeddeds and server treats cookie as secondary.

Sam (Eng): Agree. I'll include both follow-ups in the PR description.

Maria (Support): Closing loop here for now. Will report back after canary.
